comment: I took both MATH 329 and MATH 330 with Dr. Kvam. His courses are very clear, interesting, and easy to follow. His courses provided me strong foundation for studying statistics in the future career. Moreover, he is very kind and caring, always answering each question with great patience.
A very kind, caring, and intelligent professor :)

Dr. Kvam is an excellent professor and clearly very passionate about teaching. I was in MATH 329 and 330.  He provides a blank workbook; this makes studying the material efficient and is something that all profs should consider.  As a graduating UR math major, I can confidently say that Kvam's classes are among the best in the math department.

I took two statistics courses with Dr. Kvam. He is passionate about this field and motivates me to continue studying statistics in grad school. Dr. Kvam is patient in explaining the concept and his lectures are not hard to follow.

This class wasn't difficult but it wasn't a walk in the park. However if you put in the work, you could do well. He provides enough examples and materials to learn from as well. He is also incredibly understanding if you talk to him so I appreciated that as well.

Dr. Kvam is a great professor who cares about his student and can explain the content very clearly. Probability is fundamental to many future advanced domains, such as business, finance, and data science. I am very happy that I took Dr. Kvam's probability class, which has greatly helped me through my academic and career development.

Dr. Kvam is clear, engaging, and a great person/mentor. He's happy to help when you come to him. MATH329 was a pretty tough topic, but I he understood and taught with that in mind - his pacing and language were helpful. Also, his materials outside of class and assignments were well-made and thorough, so if you miss a class you can always keep up.

Dr. Kvam's probability class was very well structured and the material was engaging. The exams are exactly what was covered in the class, no surprises. There can be a lot to learn during a lecture. You will usually need to study the textbook or the videos yourself to do the homework. Overall, great experience.

I took several courses with Dr.Kvam and enjoyed my experience. Math 329 in particularly give you a good introduction to the probability world. The exam and homework have very reasonable difficulties. Dr.Kvam is a kind and caring professor, very approachable in his office hour. Would recommend this course to others

Excellent course! The course content is very helpful as an intro class for probability and the professor is nice and caring. He is very accessible outside class, so just go to his office hours or email him if you have any questions. Exams are not hard as long as you study the workbook and do the practice exams.

Dr.Kvam is always well-prepared for classes. The grading and assignments are also very clear and useful. He is also very accessible outside the class for office hours and very patient in explaining every question. He is also a nice person, always willing to form meaningful connections with students! You can get good grades if investing enough time!

Great professor! He was very caring throughout the semester. After taking this class with Dr. Kvam, I built a deep intuition and theory behind probabilities. Recommend to everyone who is not scared of taking a really interesting challenge. You won't regret it!
While Probability is not an easy course, Dr. Kvam made sure to ease things by showing the math thoroughly. He is always there to help whenever a problem gets confusing.

Math 329 is one of my favorite classes at UR. Dr. Kvam is very knowledgeable. Instead of simply going over lecture materials (which by the way are of high quality and well organized), he shows and teaches you how a statistician would approach these statistical concepts. I became super interested in statistics after taking his course.
Dr. Kvam is super approachable outside of class. If you are ever struggling with the homework or want to make sure you are ready for a test, he will spend as much time as you need to help.

Had a great time! Paul's lectures are always laid out nicely, so they were usually easy listening. Homeworks always go beyond lectures, but I think they were pretty cool and useful in hindsight. This prepares you for tests, which were way easier by comparison. Now in AI/ML, I appreciate the class even more! Also super-chill guy and cares a lot! :D

I took Math 329 with Prof Kvam during covid. The class was lecture heavy. However, working on the exercise book questions help a lot. Prof Kvam is very caring, and always made time available for office hour appointments.
Professor Kvam is great. Really enjoy taking his class. All the handouts are straight forward and really helpful. Workload is acceptable but definitely probability is not an easy topic.
Professor Kvam is so caring and always available outside of class to help with students! The class material is not that hard, so definitely recommend!

Though I took an online course MATH 329 with Dr. Kvam because of the pandemic, his course was challenging but interesting. I was especially fascinated by those distributions and greatly benefited from the applications of randomness and random processes I learnt in this course.

Dr. Kvam is very accessible outside of the class and can help you work on HW questions step by step. Class materials are very structured as he wrote the textbook himself with blank spaces for you to take notes easily. We do have 4 exams but he will give you old exams to practice, which basically cover all questions you may see in your exam.

Dr. Kvam is a very nice person and very accessible outside of class. Exams are super easy and he gives a lot of partial credits. The only problem is that he really doesn't explain things well in class. You need to study the textbook yourself to do the homework. All homework needs to be typed in LaTeX, which takes some time.

Dr. Kvam is a very average professor. His lectures are not awful but don't help a lot either. Attendance is not mandatory, but it probably helps going so that you see the sections he focuses on. The textbook will be your savior. HW is hard and time-consuming, but the exams are much easier. Plus, he gives practice exams with solutions to prepare you
Awful. Just Awful. Practically taught myself throughout the whole semester. Sorry Kvam. That was just the truth.

He is probably one of the most confusing professors I've ever had. Managed to get an A but his lectures didn't play a big part in that. I had try to read the textbook over and over to understand what's going on. He's nice sometimes but he could be condescending at other times.

His lecture is pretty confusing most of the times. He obviously knows what he is teaching but it is really hard to follow his lecture. Reading the textbook before class is crucial. However the test is pretty easy and as long as you read the textbook you will get an A in this course.

5 tests and a final. The questions on the tests are totally different from what you are "taught" in lecture or in the homeworks. Does not teach the material in an effective way. Unless you have taken a statistics class before I would avoid this professor
